note: Curated waypoint descriptions, keyed by the stable ids in data/waypoint-ids.json. Applied by scripts/build-trails.ts (overriding any description from the GPX source) and uploadable to the comments API with scripts/upload-descriptions.ts. Listed in walking order from Bundeena to Otford. The Garie Beach campground waypoint is placed at the NSW National Parks position of the Garie Beach picnic area, where its amenities are: NPWS publishes no position for the platforms themselves. Werrong Lookout has no entry: no NSW National Parks page describes it. Sources for each fact: plans/waypoint-description-sources.md.

descriptions.name: Bundeena (1 km north)
descriptions.description: The northern end of the track, which starts at the end of Beachcomber Avenue, with parking, a toilet and a water refill point. Bundeena, about 1 km north, has a supermarket, post office and cafes, and the ferry to Cronulla, where the trains to Sydney run from; the wharf is about 1.5 km from the start of the track.

descriptions.name: Drinking water
descriptions.description: Water refill at the Beachcomber Avenue trackhead. NSW National Parks lists no drinking water along the track itself; the only other water is unpotable, at Wattamolla and Garie Beach.

descriptions.name: Garie Beach campground
descriptions.description: The Coast Track's campground for overnight walkers, at the end of the 17 km first day from Bundeena, booked in advance with limited capacity. Each site is a raised timber platform for two small one-person tents or one two-person tent. The shared amenities are at the Garie Beach picnic area, where this point is placed: untreated water, cold beach showers and flush toilets.

descriptions.name: Otford Lookout
descriptions.description: Lookout and car park on Lady Wakehurst Drive at the southern end of the coast walk, with views up and down the coast. The Werrong Beach track also starts here.

descriptions.name: Otford station
descriptions.description: Southern end of the track, on Georges Road, reached from the coast along the Ridge Trail. Trains run to Sydney and Wollongong.
